title: Pathiri with Fish Curry
description: Soft rice-flour flatbreads (pathiri) typical of Lakshadweep and Malabar, served with a mild coconut-milk based fish or tuna curry. A classic island breakfast combining local starch and fresh catch.
ingredients: Rice flour, water, salt for pathiri
Coconut milk, onion, green chilli, curry leaves, mild spices
steps: Knead soft rice-flour dough and roll into thin pathiris; cook on a hot tawa.
Prepare a light coconut-milk fish curry with aromatics and curry leaves.
Serve hot pathiris with the fish curry.
tips: Pathiri in Lakshadweep is often softer and paired specifically with coconut-based fish curries.

title: Kiraliappam
description: Rice-flour pancake dipped or served with coconut milk, a traditional Minicoy/Lakshadweep breakfast item often enjoyed with spicy fish curry (rairiha) on the side.
steps: Make a smooth rice-flour batter.
Cook thin pancakes on a greased pan.
Serve dipped in or accompanied by fresh coconut milk.
tips: Commonly paired with red fish curry in Minicoy households.

title: Farata with Rairiha
description: Rectangular maida (refined flour) parathas cooked until golden, traditionally eaten in Minicoy with rairiha — a fiery red tuna or fish curry. A distinctive Minicoy breakfast combination.
ingredients: Maida, water, salt, oil for farata
Fresh tuna or fish, Kashmiri chilli, coconut milk or water, spices for rairiha
steps: Knead soft dough, roll into rectangular faratas and cook on a pan with oil until golden.
Prepare a spicy red fish curry (rairiha) with chilli and aromatics.
Serve hot faratas with the curry.
tips: Rairiha is characteristically red and spicier than everyday coconut curries.

title: Tuna Curry (Mas Riha style)
description: Fresh tuna (or skipjack) simmered in coconut milk with curry leaves, green chillies and mild spices. The everyday island staple reflecting the strong coconut-and-fish foundation of Lakshadweep (and shared Minicoy-Maldivian) cuisine.
ingredients: Onion, garlic, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves
Turmeric, mild chilli, salt, coconut oil
steps: Sauté aromatics and curry leaves in coconut oil.
Add spices and thin coconut milk; bring to a simmer.
Add tuna and cook gently.
Finish with thick coconut milk. Serve with rice or pathiri.
tips: Use the freshest tuna possible; do not overcook.

title: Kallummakaya Curry (Mussel Curry)
description: Fresh mussels cooked in a coconut-milk gravy with herbs and curry leaves. A popular seafood curry of the islands, often paired with appam or rice.
ingredients: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, ginger-garlic
steps: Clean mussels thoroughly.
Sauté aromatics and curry leaves.
Add coconut milk and spices; simmer.
Add mussels and cook until shells open and meat is done.
tips: Discard any mussels that do not open during cooking.

title: Coconut Rice
description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk, a simple yet essential accompaniment to almost every meal in Lakshadweep. Highlights the islands’ coconut monoculture.
ingredients: Salt, optional curry leaves or mild tempering
steps: Wash rice and cook in a mixture of coconut milk and water with salt.
Optional light tempering of curry leaves.
Serve as a base for curries or stews.
tips: The coconut milk gives a subtle sweetness and richness.

title: Kadala Curry
description: Black chickpeas cooked in a roasted coconut and spice gravy. One of the more substantial vegetarian options available on the islands, often influenced by Kerala styles.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, coconut oil
steps: Cook soaked chickpeas until tender.
Roast and grind coconut with spices into a paste.
Temper and combine with the chickpeas; simmer to thicken.
Serve with rice, pathiri or puttu-style sides.
tips: A reliable vegetarian main when seafood is not desired.

title: Kavaratti Biryani
description: Festive biryani from Kavaratti featuring basmati rice, fish or meat, coconut, coriander and a touch of saffron. A special-occasion dish reflecting Arab-Malabar influences on the islands.
ingredients: Coconut milk or grated coconut, onion, spices, saffron
steps: Marinate and partially cook the protein.
Prepare fragrant rice with whole spices and coconut notes.
Layer and dum-cook until flavours meld.
Garnish and serve.
tips: Fish biryani is especially characteristic of the islands.

title: Octopus Fry / Kakka Irachi Ularthiyathu
description: Tender octopus pieces stir-fried or dry-roasted with spices, coconut and curry leaves. A distinctive island seafood preparation that showcases local lagoon catch.
ingredients: Onion, green chilli, curry leaves, grated coconut
Chilli powder, turmeric, pepper, coconut oil
steps: Clean and tenderise octopus if needed.
Sauté aromatics and spices in coconut oil.
Add octopus and cook until tender and well-coated.
Finish with grated coconut and curry leaves.
tips: Overcooking can make octopus rubbery; watch the timing.

title: Mus Kavaab
description: Boneless fish cooked with grated coconut and a blend of spices into a flavourful semi-dry or curry-style preparation. A renowned Lakshadweep delicacy best eaten with rice or parotta.
ingredients: Grated coconut, onion, tomato, curry leaves
steps: Marinate fish lightly.
Prepare a coconut-spice mixture.
Cook fish with the mixture and aromatics until flavours combine.
Serve hot.
tips: Balances the natural sweetness of coconut with gentle spice.

title: Banana Chips
description: Crisp deep-fried slices of raw banana seasoned with salt, turmeric and sometimes chilli. A ubiquitous local snack reflecting South Indian and island frying traditions.
ingredients: Coconut oil or any neutral oil
steps: Peel and thinly slice raw bananas.
Deep-fry in hot oil until crisp and golden.
Drain and season with salt and turmeric.
Cool and store in an airtight container.
tips: Best when made fresh; popular with both locals and visitors.

title: Fish Pakora
description: Boneless fish pieces coated in a spiced gram-flour batter and deep-fried until crisp. A popular island snack that highlights the daily fresh catch.
ingredients: Besan (gram flour), turmeric, chilli powder, salt
steps: Marinate fish lightly with salt and turmeric.
Prepare a thick besan batter with spices.
Coat fish pieces and deep-fry until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with chutney or lemon.
tips: Use firm fish so the pieces hold shape while frying.

title: Kinnathappam
description: Steamed coconut cake or sweet pudding-like preparation made with rice and coconut. A traditional island sweet that showcases local coconut abundance.
ingredients: Fresh grated coconut or coconut milk
steps: Prepare a batter of rice and coconut with sweetener.
Pour into a steaming vessel or mould.
Steam until set and cooked through.
Cool slightly and cut or serve as is.
tips: A gentle, coconut-forward dessert or tea-time item.
